claims.claim: The Haber-Bosch process runs at roughly 200 bar (about 200 atmospheres) and temperatures up to about 500 C over an iron catalyst.
claims.episode_span: fixes nitrogen by reacting it with hydrogen at roughly 200 atmospheres and 400–500 °C over an iron catalyst
claims.supporting_quote: Most plants continue to use the original Haber process ( 20 MPa (200 bar; 2,900 psi) and 500 °C (932 °F) ), albeit with improved single-pass conversion and lower energy consumption

claims.claim: Ammonia synthesis from nitrogen and hydrogen is exothermic (delta-H about -92.28 kJ per mole of N2, which works out to roughly 2.7 GJ released per ton of ammonia).
claims.episode_span: combining nitrogen and hydrogen into ammonia is exothermic, releasing about 2.7 GJ per ton
claims.supporting_quote: This reaction is exothermic but disfavored in terms of entropy because four equivalents of reactant gases are converted into two equivalents of product gas

claims.claim: The reversible (Gibbs free-energy) minimum for water electrolysis is 237 kJ of electrical energy per mole of water, equivalent to about 33 kWh per kilogram of hydrogen.
claims.episode_span: produced by electrolysis at the reversible minimum of about 33 kWh per kilogram of H₂ — the free-energy floor
claims.supporting_quote: The electrolysis of water in standard conditions requires a theoretical minimum of 237 kJ of electrical energy input to dissociate each mole of water, which is the standard Gibbs free energy of formation of water

claims.claim: 39.4 kWh per kilogram is the higher heating value (HHV) of hydrogen -- the energy the gas holds -- not the reversible minimum work of electrolysis.
claims.episode_span: the often-quoted 39.4 kWh figure is hydrogen's heating value, not a minimum
claims.supporting_quote: commercial electrolysis requires around 53 kWh of electricity to produce one kg of hydrogen, which holds 39.4 kWh ( HHV ) of energy

claims.claim: Roughly three-quarters of world ammonia hydrogen feedstock comes from natural gas via steam reforming (72% as of 2012), consistent with the digest's 70-80% figure.
claims.episode_span: roughly 70–80 % of the hydrogen feedstock still comes from methane
claims.supporting_quote: As of 2012, the global production of ammonia produced from natural gas using the steam reforming process was 72%

claims.claim: Carl Bosch developed the industrial high-pressure apparatus for Haber's ammonia synthesis around 1913 (Nobel Prize in Chemistry 1931).
claims.episode_span: The Haber-Bosch process, commercialized in the 1910s, fixes nitrogen by reacting it with hydrogen
claims.supporting_quote: Around 1913 Carl Bosch developed an apparatus that employed different types of steel with varying resistances to pressure and heat to create an efficient process.

claims.claim: The Haber process runs at about 200 atmospheres — a compromise pressure chosen on economic grounds — and 400-450 °C over an iron catalyst.
claims.episode_span: fixes nitrogen by reacting it with hydrogen at roughly 200 atmospheres and 400–500 °C over an iron catalyst
claims.supporting_quote: 200 atmospheres is a compromise pressure chosen on economic grounds. If the pressure used is too high, the cost of generating it exceeds the price you can get for the extra ammonia produced.

claims.claim: Steam reforming of natural gas is the dominant hydrogen route: 95% of US hydrogen is made by natural gas reforming in large central plants.
claims.episode_span: a steady supply of hydrogen made by steam-reforming natural gas
claims.source_title: Hydrogen Production: Natural Gas Reforming - U.S. Department of Energy
claims.supporting_quote: Today, 95% of the hydrogen produced in the United States is made by natural gas reforming in large central plants.

claims.claim: The global fleet of ammonia plants consumed about 36 GJ per ton of ammonia (2014 benchmark, down from 37.5 GJ in 2003); a best-available-technology gas-fed plant needs 28-29 GJ per ton.
claims.episode_span: A typical modern plant consumes tens of gigajoules of energy per ton of ammonia produced
claims.source_title: Ammonia technology portfolio: optimize for energy efficiency and carbon efficiency - Ammonia Energy Association
claims.supporting_quote: Between the first benchmark (2003) and the latest one (2014), the energy consumption of the global fleet of ammonia plants dropped from 10.42 MWh to 10.00 MWh (37.5 GJ to 36 GJ) per ton ammonia.

claims.claim: Delivered (retail) anhydrous ammonia in Illinois has averaged $737 per ton since 2012 and approached $1,000 per ton in March 2026 — several hundred dollars per ton and tracking natural-gas prices.
claims.episode_span: carries a delivered price that can exceed several hundred dollars per metric ton
claims.source_title: Nitrogen Prices Remain in Focus After Iran Conflict - farmdoc daily
claims.supporting_quote: Recently, average retail anhydrous ammonia prices in Illinois have approached $1,000 per ton, well above the historical average of $737 per ton.
